cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Say You’re Sorry
cards.instruction: Maneuver someone into apologizing without naming the offense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I've put your usual mug out. We can still have tea. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Still? Are you cross with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'm hoping you won't leave me cross.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry you feel that way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you try one where you're sorry about yourself? I'll keep the tea warm.

mechanism: A presents reconciliation as something A can manage while softening and adapting the requested apology to keep B engaged, without naming the underlying offense.
confusable: Distinguish helpless pleading or unilateral demands from confident repair leadership visibly dependent on B willingness; do not name the original offense.
comparison: Tea repair negotiates a non-apology into ownership; parents arrival negotiates text symbols into a spoken sentence.
seedUse: Use canonical tea and parents seeds; borrow S02 face-saving accommodation rather than append authority claims that do not affect apology negotiation.
